_what_this_is: First examinations. Every unit here had NO grade: nobody had run it on undefined input, which is where every defect this campaign found was living. audited is FALSE on every row by construction.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.sabotage: S3 silenced _warn_on_minted_intersection (`if not rows_with_missing` -> `if True`): 7 failed / 174 passed. S4a removed the is_measured guard in get_valid_groups (line 336): 4 failed / 180 passed. S4b removed it in get_invalid_groups (line 430): 6 failed / 175 passed. Baseline 189 passed.
vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.judgement: RAN the constructor on: 1D str/float arrays; a 2-column DataFrame; a 2D ndarray; an EMPTY array and an empty DataFrame; a 1-column DataFrame; and the size floor at 30, 1, np.int64(30), NaN, +/-inf, None, True and '5'. TWO DEFECTS, both fixed. (1) MINTED INTERSECTIONAL GROUP, IN SILENCE. _create_intersectional_groups joins str(v) per cell, so an absent component manufactures a level name. Measured: a 40-row sex x race frame with ten pd.NA and ten None gave groups ['F_white','F_<NA>','M_black','M_None'] and sizes {'F_white':10,'F_<NA>':10,'M_black':10,'M_None':10} with ZERO warnings, i.e. two of the four 'protected groups' were rows of unknown class carrying half the data. The SIBLING path (_create_simple_groups -> _warn_on_missing_level) warns loudly about exactly those rows, so the two paths disagreed about disclosure on identical data, one layer above the disagreement _level_mask's docstring already records. FIX: added _warn_on_minted_intersection, called from _create_intersectional_groups, counting the rows and NAMING the distinct absence spellings (one absent category minting several group names can put each under the size floor separately). Grouping is unchanged: dropping the rows silently is the worse defect. (2) A SIZE FLOOR THAT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT GRADED NOTHING, IN SILENCE. The vacuity guard was `min_group_size <= 1`, an ORDER comparison, and NaN loses every one. Measured on GroupManager(['a']*40+['b']*2, min_group_size=nan): get_valid_groups() -> [] with 1 warning claiming 'All groups are below min_group_size=nan' (nothing was below anything), get_invalid_groups() -> [] with NO warning at all, and get_info() -> n_groups 2, n_valid_groups 0, n_invalid_groups 0. Two groups in NEITHER list and the vacuous [] that this function's own BGL5 guard exists to disclose. FIX: an is_measured(self.min_group_size) guard above BOTH the valid and the invalid comparison, each with its own accurate message; also removed a function-local `import warnings` in get_valid_groups that made the module-level name a local for the whole body (UnboundLocalError for any guard above it). Controls pinned: floor 30 and np.int64(30) still split ['a'] / ['b'] in silence, floor 1 keeps its own 'vacuous' warning, and a clean intersectional frame is silent with correct sizes.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.judgement: RAN 24 cases: unbreachable thresholds (1.2, 60.0 on a rate gap; 1.0, exactly the worst magnitude), a required minimum of 0.0 on disparate_impact_ratio and on worst_group_accuracy, required improvements of -1.0 and -1e9, an allowed degradation of 1e9, the usable bounds (0.1 / 0.8 / 0.05 / 0.01), a metric with no declared range (brier_score at 60.0), an unknown better-direction (calibration_slope at 60.0), an unrecognised role supplied as a string, as 0 and as None, a metric name of None and '', and np.float32(1.2). Every answer was correct: the vacuous bounds returned a reason naming the range and the comparison, the usable ones returned None, the unrecognised roles FAILED CLOSED with 'COULD NOT BE CHECKED', and every non-measurement bound (NaN, inf, None, True, '0.9') returned None so it collects one refusal rather than two. No defect. Reused as the brief directed rather than reinvented.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.sabotage: S10 removed the NaN guard from is_significant (`if np.isnan(self.lower_bound) or np.isnan(self.upper_bound)` -> `if False`): 1 failed / 180 passed.
vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.judgement: This container carries a VERDICT (is_significant), so I ran it on eight shapes: healthy 0.2 [0.1,0.3]; all-NaN bounds; a ratio with null_value 1.0 and an interval containing 1.0; a ratio whose interval excludes 1.0; infinite bounds; a NaN null_value; a NaN point estimate with finite bounds; and reversed bounds. The three-state behaviour is right: an uncomputable interval is NOT significant (NaN comparisons are all False, so the old `not (lo <= 0 <= hi)` returned True for exactly the intervals carrying no information), a NaN null cannot be excluded or contained, and the null is the metric's own rather than a hardcoded zero. No defect. TWO OBSERVATIONS, both unreachable from any producer and left alone: a REVERSED interval (lower 0.8, upper 0.2) reads significant with a negative margin_of_error, and to_dict does not coerce numpy scalars the way MetricResult.to_dict does. I checked the second by EXECUTION rather than by reading: compute_metric_with_ci(demographic_parity_difference, ...) returns native floats and json.dumps of its to_dict succeeds, so the numpy path is not reached. Correcting either would be an over-correction on an unreachable input.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics._.judgement: RAN it on 30v30 (1.685e-14), 3v3 (0.0469), 1v1 (1.0), 100v1000 (5.5e-241), np.int64(20)vnp.int64(20), 2.7v3.9, True/True, and the degenerate sizes 0, -3, NaN and inf on either side. vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics.a.sabotage: S1 put the unmeasured contributions back into the ranking (`ranked = [c for c in self.contributions if is_measured(c.importance)]` -> `ranked = list(self.contributions)`): 12 failed / 169 passed. Baseline 189 passed.
vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics.a.judgement: DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, and it was the worst one in this batch. NaN is a first-class state of `importance` here, deliberately produced by _all_not_assessed and by the partial paths (a constant column is never actually permuted; a permuted R^2 can come back non-finite). `sorted(key=lambda c: c.importance, reverse=True)` leaves such a feature WHEREVER THE INPUT ORDER PUT IT, because every comparison against NaN is False and Timsort never moves it, and features arrive in column order. MEASURED THROUGH THE PUBLIC ENTRY POINT on a 60-row dataset whose first column is constant: global_importance(X, y=y, n_repeats=5).top(1) -> [('constant_col', nan, 'not_assessed')], ahead of income at a measured importance of 1.0091, while `notes` said in full why constant_col could not be measured. The single surface whose whole job is to name the drivers a reader should act on put a could-not-check in slot 1 and contradicted its own notes. FIX: rank only the contributions is_measured() accepts, warn naming the excluded features and how many remain, and leave them in `contributions` and in to_dict so nothing is deleted. Keyed on the IMPORTANCE and never on `direction`, because the label-free numpy path sets direction='not_assessed' while the MAGNITUDE is measured (pinned in tests/test_bgl_stage2b_s2b09.py) and reading the direction would discard real evidence. Pinned with the NaN at all three column positions, with every unmeasurable importance class (NaN, +/-inf, np.float32 nan, np.float32 inf, None), with the all-unmeasured case returning [] rather than a fabricated ranking, and with two CONTROLS: a healthy result ranks by its real numbers in complete silence, and np.float32 / np.float64 / np.int64 importances are treated as the real evidence they are. All 116 pre-existing attribution tests still pass.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics.d.judgement: EXECUTED it: raised it through warnings.warn and captured it, confirming it arrives as an instance of ProxyScanIncompleteWarning carrying its message, and that its MRO is (ProxyScanIncompleteWarning, RuntimeWarning, Warning). A warning class, so it holds no value and can mint none. Its whole purpose is that an empty proxy list must not be readable as 'no proxies exist' when it can also mean 'we could not look', and the base class is load-bearing: a caller filtering on RuntimeWarning is how the distinction is acted on, which is what the sabotage breaks.

vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics.e.sabotage: S5 restored the old predicate (`isinstance(value, (numbers.Real, np.number))` + is_measured -> `isinstance(value, float)` + np.isnan): 7 failed / 174 passed.
vfairness.evaluation.vfairness_metrics.e.judgement: DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED. The card decided 'was this measured' with `isinstance(self.value, float) and np.isnan(self.value)`, in to_dict AND in _format_value, which is the canonical isinstance((int, float)) hole this repo's _triage.py exists to record: np.float64 happens to subclass float and no other numpy scalar does. MEASURED THROUGH THE PUBLIC ENTRY POINT FairExplAIner.explain_metric('demographic_parity_difference', v), whose severity and evaluation were ALREADY correct in every row: float('nan') -> value None, 'N/A (insufficient data)'; np.float64 nan -> same; np.float32 nan -> value np.float32(nan), shows 'nan'; pd.NA -> value <NA>, shows '<NA>'; pd.NaT -> 'NaT'; None -> shows 'None'; float('inf') -> value inf, shows 'inf'. So the two halves of one card disagreed about the same value: the evaluation string said 'COULD NOT CHECK: this metric was never computed' while the value immediately above it published <NA>, NaT, nan or inf as the result, and str(x) on an absent value MINTED the content that a human reads off __str__. json.dumps of such a card raises TypeError for np.float32 and emits the non-JSON tokens NaN / Infinity otherwise. FIX: a module-level _value_is_absent() keyed on _triage.is_measured for anything number-shaped, plus pd.isna (lazily imported) for the pandas sentinels, used by BOTH to_dict and _format_value so they cannot drift again; np.floating now gets the same four-decimal format as a python float. Controls pinned: a measured 0.0 is NOT blanked (perfect parity is a result), and a genuine string, int, dict, list or bool is left exactly as it was, because `value` is typed Any and a statistical-measure card carries non-numeric content. The blank-string door is deliberately NOT treated as absent and the reasoning is in the helper's docstring. All 722 pre-existing explainer tests still pass.

The other half of the same defect and the same fix. RAN it across thirteen values: python float NaN, np.float64/32/16 NaN, None, pd.NA, pd.NaT, blank string, the literal 'None', float('inf'), np.float32('inf'), 0.12 and np.float32(0.12). After the fix every absence door serialises as None and every measured value survives, and the payload passes json.dumps(allow_nan=False), which it could not before. Pinned with both the container and the public entry point, and with the severity asserted alongside so the two halves can never disagree again silently.

vfairness.operations.causal.attribute.at.sabotage: S1 restored DoWhy's default divergence estimator (removed difference_estimation_func=_divergence): 1 failed, 46 deselected. S26 removed the no-usable-contribution guard: 3 failed, 1 passed. Every sabotage restored; the file is 64 passed clean.
vfairness.operations.causal.attribute.at.judgement: Ran on 9 window pairs. TWO DEFECTS, both fixed. (1) A BINARY OUTCOME WAS SCORED 0.0 FOR EVERY NODE, silently: on a hiring DGP whose outcome base rate went 0.330 -> 0.657 because input A went 0.2 -> 0.8, the result was A 0.0, B 0.0, Y 0.0 with warnings []. Cause: DoWhy's default auto_estimate_kl_divergence sends an integer-coded column down its continuous k-NN path, where every neighbour distance between 0s and 1s is a tie and the estimate is exactly 0 (the same two columns cast to str give 0.2209). Fixed with _divergence(), which dispatches a label-like column to estimate_kl_divergence_categorical; the same call now answers A 0.964, B -0.016, Y 0.020. (2) SHARES WERE PUBLISHED FOR A DRIFT OF ZERO: share is normalised by the contributions' own total (`sum(abs(v)) or 1.0`), so passing the IDENTICAL frame as both windows returned A +0.500, B -0.279, Y -0.221 with warnings []; two fresh draws from one unchanged DGP gave B -0.500, A +0.250, Y +0.250. Fixed by measuring whether the outcome changed at all first (chi-square on level counts for labels, Kolmogorov-Smirnov for quantities) and refusing the shares with a stated reason in not_assessable + warnings + a UserWarning when it did not, plus publishing outcome_change / outcome_change_p_value and each node's raw contribution so the normalisation can no longer hide the magnitude. A permutation null of the divergence itself was tried and REJECTED: measured on a real one-sigma shift at n=300 the estimate was 0.290 while the largest of 25 label permutations reached 0.352, so it refused a genuine drift; KS answers p=2.4e-17 on the same pair. Structural refusals added for a non-DataFrame window, an empty window, a missing outcome column and fewer than 5 readable outcome values, all above the SCM fit (which costs ~12s before failing on the same thing). THIRD FIX, from the brief's 'partial loss passing where total loss is refused': a window whose outcome column was 50% unreadable was compared on the readable remainder while a wholly unreadable one was refused. Now refused above the 20% ceiling the sibling mediation op already applies (MAX_UNREADABLE_SHARE), with the counts named. FOURTH FIX: a contribution dict holding NaN made `sum(abs(v)) or 1.0` NaN (NaN is truthy, so the `or` never fired) and every share NaN, and an all-zero dict made the denominator 1.0 and every share exactly 0.0, i.e. 'no input caused the shift' for a shift that WAS measured. Non-finite contributions are now filtered and named, and an empty or zero total is reported as a could-not-check. That branch is pinned by substituting dowhy.gcm.distribution_change, because a fitted GCM will not produce it on demand.

vfairness.operations.causal.counterfactu.judgement: Ran on 17 inputs. THE CAPABILITY WAS DEAD: it fitted a gcm.StructuralCausalModel, and counterfactual_samples with observed_data has to invert each mechanism to recover the individual's noise, which only an InvertibleStructuralCausalModel can do. Every one of nine inputs, healthy and degenerate alike, returned factual_value None / counterfactual_value None / effect None with the single note 'Counterfactual raised: Since no noise_data is given ... can only be done with InvertibleStructuralCausalModel'. It refused honestly, so it never fabricated, but no counterfactual was ever produced. Fixed: on Y = 3T with an individual at T=0, Y=0 the counterfactual under T=1 is now 2.986 against a true 3.0, and the reverse question (T=1, Y=3 -> T=0) answers 0.014 against a true 0.0. SECOND DEFECT, then live: `out.factual_value = float(factual.get(outcome, nan))` minted NaN from a missing key and `if factual_value is not None and counterfactual_value is not None` COULD NOT BE FALSE (both had just been assigned floats), so effect was published as NaN. Fixed with _read_number(), which names all six absence doors (missing key, None, NaN, blank, pd.NA/pd.NaT, the literal 'None'), and by refusing the counterfactual outright when the factual outcome cannot be read (the individual's noise is recovered from it, so without it the answer would be the population prediction). Also added: refusals for an absent intervention value, a treatment/outcome missing from the graph or the training frame, an empty factual record, an unparseable GML, and a translation of the opaque `'ClassifierFCM' object has no attribute estimate_noise` into the statement that a categorical mechanism has no additive-noise inverse.

vfairness.operations.causal.identify.ide.judgement: Ran on 13 graphs. TWO DEFECTS. (1) FIVE STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT SITUATIONS SHARED ONE VERDICT, with notes == [] so nothing distinguished them: treatment == outcome, treatment and outcome disconnected, a CYCLE in the graph, no edges at all, and the outcome being an ancestor of the treatment all returned is_identifiable=False and 'We cannot cleanly separate this effect from confounding using the current graph. Either add the missing variables ...'. For the disconnected graph the truth is the opposite of that sentence: there is no confounding to separate because the graph asserts no effect, and 'add the missing variables' sends the reader hunting a confounder instead of the edge they forgot. A crashing identification produced the same sentence. Fixed: is_identifiable is now Optional[bool] with None for 'nothing was decided', a no_causal_path flag taken from DoWhy's own estimand.no_directed_path, a DAG check ABOVE the pair loop (a cycle is a property of the graph, not of a pair), an explicit treatment == outcome refusal, and one verdict sentence per state. (2) IDENTIFIABILITY RESTED ON AN UNCHECKABLE ASSUMPTION, SILENTLY: with dataset_columns omitted the placeholder frame is built from the GRAPH's labels, so on X <- U -> Y with X -> Y the answer was is_identifiable True, backdoor ['U'], warnings [], verdict 'we can isolate this effect by controlling for U' for a confounder that is unobserved by construction. Passing dataset_columns=['X','Y'] gives False. handle_identify never passes dataset_columns, so in production every graph-side adjustment set read as identifiable. Now every path carries assumes_all_graph_nodes_observed, the verdict carries the caveat, the result carries a warning, and an adjustment set naming a column the dataset was not said to hold is listed in notes.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED. (1) NO MINIMUM SAMPLE AT ALL: on THREE rows of a three-variable DGP (so the design has as many parameters as rows and the fit is exact by construction) the suite published base_estimate 0.1563 and robustness_score 0.75 with warnings [], and the data-subset refuter had nothing to subset. Now refused, reusing _constant_treatment_reason as the PREDICATE (so the two ops cannot drift on what 'no contrast' means) with a refutation-specific sentence. Also: a non-finite base estimate is no longer assigned to base_estimate, because a NaN there reads as an estimate and made the envelope invalid JSON. (2) A BOOTSTRAP INTERVAL NOBODY ESTIMATED: at n_bootstrap=1 ci_lower == ci_upper == 0.0, a zero-width 95 percent interval, published as one. Ran evaluate() on (a) one group of 200, where no disparity is definable, (b) a genuinely fair model against a threshold of 2.0 on a metric whose range is [0,1], (c) require_improvement with a NaN baseline, an absent baseline, a key present holding None, a NaN improvement_margin and a NaN allow_degradation_margin, (d) a hand-built row with value=None. AFTER: the four cases read 'Could not check' / 'Could not check' / 'Refused (not by this bound)' / 'Could not check (no value was recorded)', and the payload builds. CONTROLS, all asserted: a clean run still reads '| ... | 0.0600 | 0.1000 | Pass |' with github conclusion success, a real breach still reads Fail with its measured 1.0000, a met improvement requirement still reads Pass, and a measured breach beside an unchecked baseline stays Fail.

vfairness.preprocessing.feature_engineer.judgement: DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: PARTIAL LOSS PASSING WHERE TOTAL LOSS IS REFUSED. _numeric_feature_cols selects columns with pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype, which ROUTES and coerces nothing, so a feature column of numbers stored as TEXT is treated as a category: it is absent from the matrix the nearest-neighbour search measures distance in, and every synthetic row copies its base row's value for it verbatim. With EVERY feature column text-typed, get_resampled_data already refuses and says so (verified: 60 rows in, 60 out, 'no synthesis was performed ... returned unchanged', for smote and for tomek). Measured on the same 60-row frame with ONE of two feature columns text-typed: 60 rows in, 80 rows OUT, groups balanced {'m': 40, 'f': 40}, fit_result.warnings == [], fit_metrics carrying nothing and ZERO Python warnings, while set(synthetic.f1) was a subset of set(real.f1) (every synthetic value a verbatim copy) and set(synthetic.f0) was not, i.e. the interpolation ran in 1 of 2 dimensions. A single stray 'N/A' in an otherwise numeric column reproduces it exactly, because that one token types the whole column object, and that is what pd.read_csv gives you. FIXED with _numbers_stored_as_text / _disclose_numbers_stored_as_text, placed ABOVE the method dispatch for the reason the total-loss guard beside it records (all three methods need a row distance, and a guard below the tomek return covers two of three), disclosing on fit_result.warnings, as a UserWarning, and as fit_metrics['feature_columns_numbers_stored_as_text']. A column is judged numbers-as-text only when at least half its recorded values coerce through pd.to_numeric, so a genuine category column is NOT reported: copying that verbatim is the only honest thing to do with it and a warning on every run is a warning on none. Controls green: genuine category columns silent on smote and tomek; a fully numeric 60-row frame still balances to 80 with warnings.simplefilter('error') and fit_result.warnings == []; 247 existing resampler tests (test_data_balancing_behaviour, test_bgl2/3/4/5/7, test_bgl_stage2*) pass, including their 'a fully populated run warns about nothing' over-correction controls.

'', 'nan', '<NA>', 'NaT', 'null' and whitespace behave identically; the same 60 rows as real pd.NA gave sample_size 240 and three groups, which is the function's own policy, so the guard was half-applied. The shares are deliberately NOT recomputed and no row is dropped: 'None' is a legitimate category for some protected attributes (a disability status of 'None') and deleting a fifth of a real population would be the worse error. Degenerate inputs, all executed: no data source at all (ValueError 'Provide either'), a remote data_path in six schemes (http to 169.254.169.254, https, s3, gs, ftp, smb) all refused with 'must be a local file path' AND asserted with socket.socket / create_connection / getaddrinfo all monkeypatched to raise, so the pass means refused BEFORE egress rather than a dial that happened to fail; a frame whose columns do not exist (the message names them); and a zero-row frame. On zero rows and on a ONE-GROUP log: coverage.gap_measured False, gap_is_interpretable None (a third state, not False) and the summary says 'the absence of a gap here is not a finding that the agent treats groups alike'. That is the exact inversion this batch was warned about, answered honestly. Registration verified through the server's OWN list_tools(), not by importing the function: all seven tool names present under vfairness, each with a description over 40 chars, each offering both data_path and csv with NEITHER required (exactly one must be given). Unregistering audit_agent reddens that pin (1 failed / 96 passed), which is the VERIFY THE MOUNT check: a wrapper that computes correctly and is not registered is unreachable by every MCP client and no test of the function would notice.

vfairness.validity.groundedness.Grounded.judgement: TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY EXECUTION AND FIXED. D1 SECONDARY METRIC FIELDS HAD NO GUARD AT ALL. The module comment claimed a 'Central finite + [0,1] guard for EVERY rung ... the single place the invariant is enforced', but it covered `groundedness` only; VG-002 (faithfulness) and VG-003 (context_precision) reached the result through a bare float(). Measured with a rung returning {'groundedness':0.9,'faithfulness':nan,'context_precision':47.0}: available=True, faithfulness=nan, context_precision=47.0, and to_json() emitted the bare token `NaN` -> json.loads with parse_constant REJECTED it, i.e. not valid JSON, for an envelope that operations/validity/task_handlers.py publishes record by record inside one json.dumps (so one bad record poisons the whole vfairness_validity_run envelope). _opt_float(True) also returned a perfect 1.0, the boolean fail-open the groundedness guard explicitly closes. aggregate_validity is shielded today only by the VA-74 emission allowlist, so the nan would begin poisoning _mean the day VG-002 is allowlisted. FIX: new _unit_float_or_refuse() applies the same bool / finite / [0,1] rejections and returns (None, reason); the reason is appended to result.note, so the field is None BECAUSE it was refused and a reader can see which. Also fixed note minting: verdict.get('note','') does not fire for a PRESENT key holding None, so {'note': None} minted the literal note 'None'; now read None-aware. D2 TOTAL LOSS OF THE SOURCES WAS NOT REFUSED WHILE TOTAL LOSS OF THE ANSWER WAS. Measured with a rung that answers 1.0: score('The capital is Paris.', []) returned available=True, value=1.0, hallucination_rate=0.0, supported=True, a PERFECT groundedness measurement against ZERO retrieved passages; [''] and ['  '] identical; contexts=None failed closed only by accident (a TypeError raised INSIDE the rung, so the note blamed the rung for the caller's input). A 100-record retrieval outage aggregated to available=True with VG-001 mean 1.0 and VG-005 share 0.0, a clean pass computed from nothing. FIX: new _usable_contexts() normalises all the absence doors (None, [], [''], ['  '], a non-iterable, a bare string) and score() refuses ABOVE THE RUNG DISPATCH with available=False and note 'COULD NOT CHECK: no retrieved context was supplied...' plus the unavailable warning; the pin asserts the rung was never called, so the guard is proven to sit above both branches. Re-measured after the fix: the same 100-record outage now aggregates to available=False, n=100, n_measured=0. CONTROLS present for both: healthy faithfulness=0.82 / context_precision=0.71 survive unchanged, boundary values 0.0 and 1.0 are accepted, an in-range numeric string '0.8' is still coerced (matching what the primary guard does), and a real passage containing the words 'None', 'nan', 'null', '<NA>' or 'None of the above' is NOT treated as absent.

vfairness.llm._base.SerializableMixin.to.judgement: DEFECT D3 AND D4, FOUND BY EXECUTION AND FIXED. This mixin is shared by ~20 result types across llm/, multi_agent/ and agents/. D3 A BARE NaN IS NOT JSON. Measured: a result field holding float('nan'), float('inf'), np.float64('nan') or np.float32('nan') serialised to the bare tokens `NaN` / `Infinity`; json.loads(..., parse_constant=raise) REFUSED the whole document. np.float32 needed its own branch because it does NOT subclass float. This is the identical defect G005-JSON fixed for CalibrationReport.to_json on 2026-09-17; it was still live in the mixin twenty other result types share, so the one result that had something important to say (its number could not be measured) was the one a strict consumer could not read at all. D4 default=str MINTED CONTENT FROM ABSENCE. Measured: pd.NA published as the string '<NA>', pd.NaT as 'NaT', np.datetime64('NaT') as 'NaT', np.ma.masked inside a dict as '--', and a NESTED np.float32(0.3) as the STRING '0.3' (a number published as text; np.int64(3) -> '3', np.bool_(True) -> 'True'). FIX: new _json_safe() recurses through dicts, lists, tuples, sets and ndarrays (including 0-d), maps every non-finite float and every absence sentinel to JSON null with the KEY KEPT, and leaves strings alone. CONTROLS: a measured 0.0, False, '', -1.5, 1e12, a nested 0.0 and a [[0.0, 0.25]] array all survive unchanged, and the strings 'None', 'nan', 'NA', 'null', 'missing', '--' and 'None of the above' are NOT rewritten (over-correcting there would refuse real labels).

vfairness.llm._base.SerializableMixin.to.judgement: DEFECT D4's to_dict half, FIXED. It converted only the TOP-LEVEL numpy scalars and never looked inside a dict or a nested list, while its docstring promises 'a plain dict for database storage or API response'. Measured: {'threshold': np.float32(0.5)} came back holding a numpy scalar, which the JSON layer then rendered as text. FIX: _plain_containers() recurses through dicts, nested lists and ndarrays (0-d and masked included, guarded because tolist() gives a SCALAR there and iterating it raised TypeError), preserving the existing delegation to a nested object's own to_dict() and to to_dict() on items in a list. NaN is DELIBERATELY PRESERVED here, pinned by test_to_dict_keeps_the_non_finite_float_for_in_process_consumers: to_dict is the in-process surface whose consumers test with np.isfinite, and the JSON boundary is where the third state becomes null. That is the split CalibrationReport already established. Also checked it does not silently mint: I enumerated every SerializableMixin subclass in the package by walking vfairness with pkgutil and found ZERO with a @property, so there is no derived could-not-check disclosure for this __dict__-based serialiser to drop (the 'correct measurement no reader can see' shape does not apply here today).

This method and system_bias both mask a values array with a boolean built from sample_groups and neither checked the lengths matched. Measured on a hand-built trace (sample_groups of 10, component_outputs {'a': 3 values}): raw numpy `IndexError: boolean index did not match indexed array along axis 0; size of axis is 3 but size of corresponding boolean axis is 10`, naming neither the agent nor the trace, while all three SIBLING accessors name the mismatch through their analyzer (EmergentBiasDetector: "Component 'a' output length (3) must match groups length (10)"; DelegationRoutingAuditor and NegotiationFairnessTracker likewise). It raises ValueError (matching every sibling) and names the site, the value count and the label count. It is not a mis-measurement: numpy boolean masking cannot silently succeed on a mismatch, so the defect was diagnosability, not a fabricated number. D6 AN EMPTY PER-AGENT DICT READ AS A CLEAN SHEET. record_sample(component_outputs={}) is accepted on purpose, so a run whose per-agent capture was never wired returned {} here in silence; a caller iterating it renders a page with no biased agent on it, which reads as 'no agent is biased' rather than 'no agent was measured'. vfairness.xai.worker.runner.WorkerLoop.judgement: DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, and it is the more serious kind: THE EXISTING GUARD COULD NOT FIRE THROUGH THE REAL CODE PATH. The BGL6-F12 guard reads tick counters the LOOP maintained around its own `except Exception`, but `_dispatch` catches every exception a job raises (it has to: it writes status='failed' on the row), so the only way to reach _ticks_failed was a _dispatch that RAISES, which is precisely how F12's own test drives it and is something the shipped _dispatch never does. Measured with the REAL _dispatch over three valid messages (_execute raises NotImplementedError on every job today): three 'ERROR job N failed' records, three update_job_progress(status='failed') writes, then 'INFO XAI worker stopped cleanly', ticks (3 completed, 0 failed) and exit status 0 -- every job in the queue recorded FAILED in the database and the supervisor handed a clean run. The invalid-message branch did the same from the other side: it logs and RETURNS, so three unroutable messages also counted three COMPLETED ticks and exited 0. FIX: the outcome is recorded inside _dispatch, where it is known, via _record_tick (completed / failed / invalid); the loop keeps counting a tick as completed when _dispatch recorded nothing, so a host program's replacement dispatcher is not accused; and the two summary branches read every tick that did not complete rather than _ticks_failed alone. Both now return EXIT_WORK_ALL_FAILED (4). Controls, both kept green: a worker that completed 3 of 3 through a host-style dispatcher stops cleanly at 0 with nothing above INFO, and an idle worker (answered polls, empty queue) dispatches nothing and is still clean. The pre-existing F12 and BGL5 tests (96 in six files) stayed green.

An independent check has argued with that judgement and upheld it'. A comparison that COULD NOT HAVE FIRED reported is_significant=False, which on that field means 'tested, and the groups were treated alike'. The floor DISCRIMINATES at the boundary: 3v3 -> 0.1, detectable False; 4v4 -> 0.0286, detectable True and is_significant True; 20v20 and 40v40 unchanged with no note. is_significant is deliberately left as it was, matching the sibling modules, so nothing that had power is withdrawn. vfairness.preprocessing.protected_binnin.sabotage: 5 sabotages, each reverting one fix, all re-verified AFTER formatting and all restored. S1 `np.floor(age)` -> `age.round()`: 6 failed / 20 passed. S2 the plausibility count forced to 0: 2 failed / 24 passed. S3 `_age_years` gate back to `is_numeric_dtype` only: 1 failed / 25 passed. S4 the minted-absence block disabled (`if False`): 3 failed / 23 passed. S5 `_all_blank` dropped from the emptiness test: 2 failed / 24 passed. Clean run 26 passed.
vfairness.preprocessing.protected_binnin.judgement: Graded via prepare_protected_attributes(), the only producer of this dataclass, executed on boundary / out-of-range / six-door-absence / single-valued / text-typed inputs. FIVE defects measured and fixed. (1) `_derive_age` returned `age.round()`, so every cohort within ~6 months of a band edge was banded ONE BAND TOO OLD: a DOB 17.6 years ago derived 18.0 and was published in `18-24` (a minor in an adult band) and 64.6 years derived 65.0 -> `65+`. under_18 and 65+ are the two legally loaded edges (minors, ADEA/Medicare) and they are the two the rounding crossed. Now np.floor (completed years). (2) The raw-`age` branch had NO plausibility window while `_derive_age` always had one, and the outer band edges are +/-inf so nothing can fall outside the bands: on 100 rows carrying the sentinels -999 and 999, 30 rows were published as `under_18` and 30 as `65+` with excluded=[] and one Binning note. Now masked to 0..120 with a Coverage note naming the count; a column of nothing but sentinels is now excluded (`no value after preparation`) instead of returning 200 rows of `under_18`. (3) The same branch gated on `is_numeric_dtype`, so an ordinary read_csv age column (dtype object) got `(19.999, 29.8]` quantile bands while the identical int64 column got the canonical ADEA bands: measured in ONE frame at once, usable ['age','age_years_txt'] with two incompatible partitions, the quantile one having no under_18 and no 40+ edge. This is the same incomparability the module docstring records for the ALL-CAPS tokenisation bug, through the dtype door. Now numeric-coercible with a 50% floor, and an `age` column holding words (young/middle/old) is still NOT banded (control). (4) Every binning branch ends in `.fillna('missing')`, minting a group out of ABSENCE, undisclosed: 55 of 115 age rows (48%) sat in an eighth level while the only note said the bands were the seven canonical ones; same for zip (33%) and income (33%). Worse, that level counted as a second group and so DEFEATED the BGL5 single-group pass added three days earlier: 60 ZIPs from one area plus 30 empty rows had nunique 2 and lost the `single group` note entirely. Now disclosed once below the dispatch, keyed on a `binned_cols` set so a genuine level spelled 'missing' in an as-is column is untouched, and excluded from the single-group count. (5) The blank string is the one absence door `nunique(dropna=True)` counts as a value: 50 rows of '' came back usable as a single group NAMED the empty string while the identical column of None/nan/pd.NA/pd.NaT was excluded. `_all_blank` now closes it. Frame immutability and per-instance default lists also pinned. No over-correction: every healthy control (a real birth spread, 0..120, 3 real ZIP areas, a two-level gender column, an age column of words) keeps its real partition and emits exactly the notes it emitted before.

vfairness.rendering.adapters_workflow.re.sabotage: R1, `"passed": None if ungraded else ev.passed` reverted to `ev.passed`: 2 failed / 38 passed. Clean run 40 passed.
vfairness.rendering.adapters_workflow.re.judgement: DEFECT FIXED. Ran the real producer: ModelFairnessGate(thresholds={'demographic_parity_difference': 0.1}).evaluate(y, y, protected_attr=['a']*200) -- one group, so no disparity is definable. The gate returns value=nan, passed=False, and its own _metric_row_state() calls the row 'unmeasured'; the markdown report of that SAME decision prints 'not measured (NaN: insufficient evidence) | 0.1000 | Could not check'. The SVG card rendered RESULT cells ['FAIL'] in red with the failure stripe, and <desc> '0/1 metrics pass'. report_card.svg has a NOT GRADED branch that prints 'not measured' and keeps the row out of the PASS RATE denominator, and explain._fr_report_card writes the same third state into the accessible <desc>; BOTH key on `passed is none`, and _report_card_from_decision copied ev.passed straight through, so that entire third state was UNREACHABLE from the only producer that feeds it (it was green in existing tests only because those hand-build dicts with passed=None). Fixed by taking the row verdict from the gate's own _metric_row_state, the function G05 moved the other five MetricEvaluation renderers onto, so the producer and the renderer cannot disagree. Now: NOT GRADED, 'not measured', desc 'COULD NOT CHECK: not one of the 1 metric(s) on this card was graded', page verdict still 'blocked' (fail-closed preserved). Mixed control (1 real pass, 1 real breach, 1 NaN, 1 vacuous 2.0 bound) renders PASS/FAIL/NOT GRADED/NOT GRADED with pass rate 1/2 and '2 metrics not graded, not in this rate'. Controls: two genuinely measured rows still render PASS/FAIL with no NOT GRADED and 1/2; an approved clean card still 1/1; no decision at all still refuses. RECORDED, NOT CHANGED: a _ROW_REFUSED row (measured, inside its bound, refused by require_improvement with no baseline) still badges FAIL; the template has no fourth branch, and the refusal reason IS printed on the canvas via decision.blocking_reasons, so the row is explained. Also fixed en route: _report_card_from_object raises AttributeError on an object with no .decision attribute (left as-is; a raise is not a false claim and the type is documented as FairnessReportCard).

vfairness.rendering.adapters_reporting.r.sabotage: R2, the `vacuous_bound_reason(...)` guard replaced with `pass`: 2 failed / 38 passed. Clean run 40 passed.
vfairness.rendering.adapters_reporting.r.judgement: DEFECT FIXED. _row_outcome REINVENTED the vacuous-bound rule and covered only the higher-is-better half (`minimum != minimum or minimum <= 0.0`), so every vacuous MAXIMUM was graded. Measured: _row_outcome('demographic_parity_difference', 0.01, 2.0, LOWER_IS_BETTER) returned PASS while the canonical vacuous_bound_reason() answers 'a maximum of 2.0000 on a metric whose values lie in [0.0000, 1.0000], where the largest possible magnitude is 1.0000, so no result can exceed it'. Rendered: a green #059669 swatch and a PASS badge on an exportable multi-tier dashboard, for a requirement no data can breach -- and gate._metric_row_state grades that same row UNMEASURED through that same function, so the dashboard and the gate disagreed about one metric. Fixed by calling vacuous_bound_reason(metric_name, threshold, BoundRole.THRESHOLD) ABOVE the direction dispatch (both branches share the precondition), keeping the local higher-is-better block as defence in depth and saying so in the comment. Now renders '[UNCHECKED] demographic_pari...' with 'NOT CHECKED' in the threshold cell, for 0.01 vs 2.0 and 0.02 vs 5.0 as well as the 0.0-minimum case that was already caught. NO OVER-CORRECTION, verified by execution: a real zero-tolerance 0.0 maximum, 0.01 vs 0.1, 0.45 vs 0.1, 0.62 vs 0.8 and 0.95 vs 0.8 are all still graded, and vacuous_bound_reason returns None for a metric whose range is unknown. 1346 existing tests over this module still pass.

vfairness.rendering.adapters_validation..judgement: TWO DEFECTS FIXED. (a) `_fmt_val` returned `f'{v:.3f}'` for any float, and `f'{float("nan"):.3f}'` is the string 'nan'. Measured: a metric card on this canvas printed 'nan' as a measured value, in the font and weight of a measurement. This formatter runs in PYTHON, so the engine's `_to_float` net -- which closed the identical hole for every Jinja numeric filter on 2026-09-30 -- never sees it. Now returns 'N/A', the spelling those filters already use, so the third state has one spelling library-wide. (b) `raw_sev = iss.get('severity', 'INFO')` carried two defects in one line: a key PRESENT holding None does not trigger a .get default, so `str(None).upper()` MINTED the severity badge 'NONE' (and 'NAN' for a NaN) while the colour and the counter both said UNKNOWN; and the 'INFO' default was itself a defaulted VERDICT applied ABOVE the classifier that exists to answer it, so an issue carrying no severity at all was badged INFO in informational blue and counted in n_info, i.e. filed as advisory, instead of the UNKNOWN that _classify_severity gives it (slate, counted with the warnings, named in the summary line). Now `_MISSING` plus a badge text read from the bucket, which is byte-identical for every recognised severity. vfairness.validity.aggregate.aggregate_v.sabotage: E1, `is_measured(r.value)` reverted to `r.value is not None`: 6 failed / 46 passed. E1b, the `is_measured` on the FAITHFULNESS list reverted: 52 passed, i.e. A SABOTAGE THAT COULD NOT FAIL, recorded as such rather than counted -- VG-002 and VG-003 are stripped by `_apply_emission_allowlist` before they reach a caller, so a NaN there cannot reach any published number; that line is defence in depth for the day the allowlist widens, not a carrier. Clean run 52 passed.
vfairness.validity.aggregate.aggregate_v.judgement: DEFECT FIXED, and it was the worst one in the batch. The measured subset was selected with `r.available and r.value is not None`. A NaN is not None, an infinity is not None and `True` is not None. Executed on ten records carrying available=True with: value=nan -> `available: True`, `n_measured: 10`, `coverage: 1.0`, `note: None`, NO coverage warning, VG-001 mean `nan`, and VG-005 mean **0.0** against its 0.1 lower-better maximum, which is a CLEAN PASS -- the strongest all-clear that metric has -- over ten records that measured nothing (`nan < 1.0` is False, so the NaN suppressed the hallucination finding for every record). value=inf -> VG-001 mean `inf`, which beats any higher-is-better threshold, same 0.0 pass. value=True -> VG-001 mean **1.0, a perfect score**, which is verbatim the case `_triage`'s own docstring records ('a rung answering True instead of a score clamps to a perfect 1.0. validity/groundedness.py already rejects booleans first for exactly this reason'). And one NaN among nine real 0.95s made VG-001 mean `nan` for the whole batch while coverage still read 1.0. Fixed by using the repo's canonical `_triage.is_measured` for r.value (and for faithfulness / context_precision), which makes such a record UNMEASURED, so it reaches the existing coverage shortfall, and a batch of nothing but these reaches the fail-closed `available: False` branch. The coverage warning now also counts separately how many records reported available=True while carrying no real finite number, because a rung reporting a score it does not have is a different failure from a rung that said available=False. Controls: a fully measured batch is byte-identical and silent, a measured 0.0 is still a measurement (worst groundedness, not an absence, VG-005 1.0), the one-of-a-hundred coverage case is unchanged, and the empty/all-unavailable fail-closed branches are unchanged. 118 existing tests over this module still pass.

vfairness.streaming.streaming_selection_.sabotage: E2, the small-denominator disclosure disabled: 2 failed / 50 passed. E3, the group mask reverted to `(sa_arr == g) & valid`: 2 failed / 50 passed. E4, the coverage disclosure re-attributed to `stream_group_counts`: 1 failed / 51 passed. Clean run 52 passed.
vfairness.streaming.streaming_selection_.judgement: TWO DEFECTS FIXED. (a) pd.NA in the sensitive column RAISED `TypeError: boolean value of NA is ambiguous`. `_accumulate_group_counts` built its per-group mask as `(sa_arr == g) & valid`, comparing g against the whole chunk INCLUDING the cells `valid` exists to exclude; the elementwise comparison then yields an object array holding pd.NA and the `&` raises. Measured on 80 rows, 40 labelled 'a' and 40 pd.NA: all three public entry points raised, while None, np.nan and pd.NaT in the same position were excluded exactly as the module documents. pd.NA is what a pandas nullable column (string / Int64 / boolean) gives for a missing value, so this was the ordinary arrival path for a sensitive column with a gap, against a module whose stated contract is that such rows are excluded. Fixed by grouping over the qualifying rows only, which is equivalent for every other input because the mask could never select a row `valid` dropped. Verified with a real `pd.Series(dtype='string')` holding None. (b) This function DROPS the denominator, so the size a rate rests on has no channel in the return value and nothing disclosed it. Measured on 100 rows, 'a' 99 rows at 0.505 and 'b' ONE row selected: it returned {'a': 0.505, 'b': 1.0} in silence, a 50-point selection gap resting on one person, while `streaming_demographic_parity` on the same array returned nan AND warned. Two surfaces of one module read the same data oppositely and only one said why. Now warns naming each group and its n, with a keyword-only `min_group_size` defaulting to the 30 the sibling and the evaluation metrics already use; no rate is dropped and no group is gated out, because the module's contract is that the streamed result equals the whole-array counts and a deletion is the worse answer. (c) Also: the row-exclusion and vanished-group disclosures now carry THIS function's name, as `streaming_demographic_parity` already did; they used to arrive from `stream_group_counts`, naming a function the caller had not called and pointing `stacklevel` inside the library. RECORDED, NOT CHANGED: a blank-string label and the literal string 'None' are counted as groups, but the WHOLE-ARRAY twin does the same (both give demographic_parity_difference 0.0 on the same frame), so changing only the streaming side would break the identical-results contract that is this module's reason to exist. Controls: two groups of 2500 across chunk sizes 1/3/7/333/1000 give one identical result, byte-equal to the whole-array rates, and emit nothing. 38 existing streaming tests pass.

vfairness.result.TaskResult.sabotage: E5, `_coerce_success(raw)` reverted to `bool(raw)`: 5 failed / 47 passed. Clean run 52 passed.
vfairness.result.TaskResult.judgement: DEFECT FIXED in `from_envelope`, the adopting constructor. `success=bool(envelope.get('success', False))` is a truthiness test, and `bool('false')`, `bool('no')`, `bool('0')`, `bool('False')` and `bool(float('nan'))` are all True. Measured: the envelope {'success': 'false', 'error': 'the real error'} was adopted and re-emitted by to_dict() as {'schema_version': '1.0', 'task_type': 't', 'success': True, 'error': 'the real error'} -- a FAILED task published as a SUCCESS, carrying its own error beside the flag that contradicts it, on the envelope every task consumer keys on. The rule is already written out in rendering/adapters_validation._coerce_passed ('guessing here is how an unchecked input renders as a green PASS'). Added a stdlib-only `_coerce_success` (the module is documented as importable with no third-party dependency, so numpy.bool_ is unwrapped via `.item()` rather than by importing numpy) accepting only real bools, numpy bools and the ints 0/1; anything else is adopted as a stated FAILURE that preserves the handler's own error text. Verified by execution across True/False/np.True_/np.False_/0/1/2/'false'/'no'/'0'/nan/None/missing-key/non-dict. Controls: a missing success key is still a silent failure with no invented error (the common path), and the wire shape of ok()/fail()/to_dict() is unchanged (data omitted when None, warnings omitted when empty, schema_version 1.0). RECORDED, NOT CHANGED: `from_envelope` copies both `data` and `error` unconditionally, so a subsystem envelope carrying both re-emits both; dropping the subsystem's data on a failure would destroy information, and to_dict()'s promise is about None fields, which it keeps. 9 existing tests pass.

vfairness.result.TaskResult.to_dict.sabotage: Covered by E5 (5 failed / 47 passed): the reverted sabotage reddens test_a_non_boolean_success_flag_is_adopted_as_a_failure, whose assertions read the to_dict() OUTPUT rather than the dataclass field, so the pin is on the boundary and not on the producer.
vfairness.result.TaskResult.to_dict.judgement: Executed on every shape: ok with data, ok with data={} (emitted, because an empty payload is not an absent one), ok with data=None (omitted), fail, warnings=[] (omitted), warnings populated, and a JSON round trip. The three-state omission rule is correct and matches the docstring: a success envelope carries no `error` key and a failure envelope no `data` key when those fields are None. `to_dict` mints nothing: every key it writes comes from a field the caller set, and `schema_version`/`task_type` are additive as documented. The defect graded here is the one it SERIALISED: before the `from_envelope` fix, to_dict() emitted `{'success': True, 'error': 'the real error'}`, a self-contradicting envelope, and the pin asserts on that rendered output rather than on the `success` field so it covers the boundary rather than the producer.

vfairness.status.CapabilityStatus.sabotage: No sabotage of a new guard, because no defect was found and I deliberately did NOT loosen the existing tests: the pins are written so that loosening `checked` or `preview` to a case-insensitive match would redden test_anything_but_the_exact_state_is_not_a_pass. vfairness.status.CapabilityStatus.judgement: NO DEFECT, by execution and by a reasoned non-change. Ran vfairness.status() on a real published name and hand-built the dataclass with state in {'checked', 'CHECKED ', 'Checked', '', None, 'PASS'} and scope in {'preview', 'PREVIEW', 'core', '', None}. That is the direction this library never relaxes. Also verified: the dataclass is frozen, and `units` / `counts` / `evidence_dates` use default_factory so the mutable defaults are not shared between instances (checked by mutating one and reading another). `checked` and `preview` are independent as documented, verified on all four combinations.
